fixes.title: Combat bonus vs different ideology is lost after load / resync
fixes.before: CvUnit::m_iCombatBonusVsDifferentIdeologyModifier is not saved. After loading a save or after a resync every unit has 0, so promotions that give a bonus against another ideology stop working and combat results differ from the uninterrupted game (peers fall into a resync loop).
fixes.after: On load the value is recomputed from the unit's (saved) promotions with the same per-promotion value that gaining a promotion adds. A loaded game behaves like the continuous one. Save format unchanged.
fixes.scope: Every CvUnit::read; only units whose promotions have CombatDifferentIdeology != 0 change (diag trigger FIX id 1 fires for them).
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: desync after any load/resync (golden peer has 0, fixed peer has the bonus).
fixes.balance: none for a continuous game; after load the intended bonus is back (a loaded game used to be weaker).
fixes.notes: No other writer of the field exists: setHasPromotion is the only SetBit on the promotion bitfield.

fixes.title: Reformation belief availability starts from garbage in a new game
fixes.before: CvPlayer::m_bCanChooseReformationBelief is neither initialised in the constructor nor reset, so a new game starts with whatever was in memory: peers could disagree about who may pick a Reformation belief.
fixes.after: The flag starts as false in the constructor and on every reset.
fixes.scope: New game / CvPlayer::reset when the old value was non-zero (diag trigger FIX id 2 fires in reset when the previous value was true; loads overwrite it from the save anyway).
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: possible desync in a new game whenever the golden peer has non-zero garbage.
fixes.notes: The member is serialized (read/write), so only new games and warm re-use of a CvPlayer were affected.

fixes.title: Italy unique ability (golden age on finishing a policy tree) applied on one machine only
fixes.before: Lekmod_italy.lua applied the golden-age turns / progress only when the local active player was the Italy owner: in multiplayer only the owner's machine got the bonus (out of sync), an AI Italy never got it.
fixes.after: The bonus is applied on every machine for every Italy owner, AI included (decision of the user). The local-player guard remains only around the on-screen alert.
fixes.scope: GameEvents.PlayerAdoptPolicy for a player with CIVILIZATION_ITALY who finishes a policy branch.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with the old Lua: desync whenever an Italy owner finishes a policy tree (one side has the bonus).
fixes.balance: AI Italy now receives the golden age bonus; for a human Italy the documented bonus is now really applied on all peers (it only ever worked on the owner's machine).
fixes.notes: Lua has no flags; the change ships with the Lua files of the build (sim-compat-id includes their hashes).

fixes.title: Consulates catch-up votes only for the first player; handler removes itself
fixes.before: Lekmod_OnAdoptConsulates called GameEvents.PlayerAdoptPolicy.Remove(itself) after the first adoption of Consulates by any player: later players received no World Congress votes for the eras already passed. After a load or resync the handler is registered again, so behaviour depended on the session and a resynced peer differed from the others.
fixes.after: The handler stays registered. The policy id check already makes it fire once per adoption.
fixes.scope: GameEvents.PlayerAdoptPolicy with POLICY_CONSULATES.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with the old Lua: desync when a second player adopts Consulates, and after a resync.
fixes.balance: Second and later players that adopt Consulates now get the catch-up league votes (+1 per passed era from Industrial on); before only the first adopter of a session did. Reported to the user; release=true because it is also a desync fix.
fixes.notes: If a policy can be re-adopted after being removed the player would get the votes again; not reachable in normal play (no policy removal path except ideology switch).

fixes.title: Player 0 never gets dummy buildings and dummy policies (ipairs(Players))
fixes.before: Players is numbered from 0 but ipairs starts at 1: the player in slot 0 (usually the host) never gets the dummy buildings / dummy policies of their civilization.
fixes.after: Slot 0 is visited like all other majors (loop 0 .. MAX_MAJOR_CIVS-1).
fixes.scope: lekmod_add_global_dummy_buildings and lekmod_add_dummy_policies, player slot 0 only.
fixes.mp_compat: Synchronous on every peer; mixed with the old Lua: desync only if slot 0 owns a civ with dummy data.
fixes.balance: Yes: the slot-0 player starts receiving the dummy bonuses of their nation (e.g. nation-specific buildings and policies) that every other slot already had.
fixes.notes: Implemented behind a local switch that is OFF, so the shipped Lua behaves like the original until the user sets it to true.

fixes.title: Dummy buildings: player object compared with a number
fixes.before: `player == player_or_team_id` compares an object with a number and is always false, so only `player:GetTeam() == id` matches. For player events (policy adopted, city founded, golden age, branch unlocked, city captured) the building refresh therefore hits the player whose TEAM id equals the player id, which is the wrong player in team games.
fixes.after: Player events match on player:GetID(), the team event (TeamSetHasTech) matches on the team.
fixes.scope: lekmod_add_global_dummy_buildings in games where team id != player id (team games, shared teams).
fixes.mp_compat: Synchronous on every peer; only team games differ.
fixes.balance: Yes, in team games: dummy buildings follow the right player.
fixes.notes: Implemented behind a local switch that is OFF (original expression kept in the else branch).

fixes.title: Dummy policies are granted from a local engine event (Events.SequenceGameInitComplete)
fixes.before: lekmod_add_dummy_policies mutates game state (SetNumFreePolicies, SetHasPolicy) from Events.*, a local engine event: it runs on every load and, after a resync, only on the resynced peer. The HasPolicy guard makes it idempotent for the dummy policy but SetNumFreePolicies(1)/(0) zeroes the free policies a player has accumulated whenever the dummy policy is missing.
fixes.after: PROPOSAL, no code: grant from a synchronous point (first GameEvents.PlayerDoTurn of each player) and keep the guard.
fixes.scope: Game start / loading a save where the dummy policy is missing.
fixes.mp_compat: Not changed (no code).
fixes.balance: The grant would shift by up to one turn; rare cases of lost free policies disappear.
fixes.notes: Not moved: timing of the grant matters for turn-0/1 processing and the change is not provably neutral. Left as a proposal for the user.

fixes.title: CvDangerPlots::UpdateDanger clears all danger plots but the last one
fixes.before: In the AUI_DANGER_PLOTS_FIX_USE_ARRAY_NOT_FFASTVECTOR branch the wipe is fill(m_DangerPlots, &m_DangerPlots[iGridSize - 1], 0): the last map cell keeps the previous turn's danger.
fixes.after: No change. That branch is dead code in v34.15: AUI_DANGER_PLOTS_FIX_USE_ARRAY_NOT_FFASTVECTOR sits inside the /* ... */ block of _Defines.h (lines 28-69) and is not defined; the compiled path is a plain loop over all iGridSize cells.
fixes.scope: none (verified with a cl /EP probe of _Defines.h)
fixes.mp_compat: n/a
fixes.notes: If that AUI switch is ever enabled, change the end iterator to m_DangerPlots + iGridSize.

fixes.title: Espionage AI counters reset to defaults on every load (arrays appended instead of read)
fixes.before: CvPlayer::Read -> reset() pre-fills the seven CvEspionageAI vectors (spies caught/killed/died, last-turn markers, out-of-tech turn) with MAX_MAJOR_CIVS defaults, then the reader appended the saved values. The game indexes entries 0..21, so after a load or resync every counter was back at its default and the saved values were dead; each save/load cycle grew every vector by 22 entries (+616 bytes per player).
fixes.after: The saved values are read over the defaults. Saves written by golden after a load carry stale extra entries: only the first MAX_MAJOR_CIVS (the ones golden was using) are kept. Save format unchanged.
fixes.scope: Every CvEspionageAI read (load, resync, hot-join); diag trigger FIX id 9. Continuous play unchanged.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: desync after any load/resync once an espionage counter is non-default (golden peer resets it, fixed peer keeps it).
fixes.balance: none for a continuous game; after a load the espionage AI keeps its memory of caught/killed spies.
fixes.notes: Round-trip check: player00..63 +616 bytes each after one load (golden), clean with the fix.

fixes.title: Ancient-ruin memory scrambled on every load (read order differs from write order)
fixes.before: With LEKMOD_NEW_ANCIENT_RUIN_REWARDS, CvGoodyHuts::Write stores all players' recent-goody arrays and then all players' once-per-game flags, but Read interleaved them per player. After a load the recent goodies of players 1+ came from flag values (-1/0: goody 0 looked 'recently received') and the once-per-game flags from goody ids.
fixes.after: Read uses Write's order. Save format unchanged; version 0 saves (no once-per-game block) load as before.
fixes.scope: Every ReadSupportingClassData of a version-1 goody block; diag trigger FIX id 10. Continuous play unchanged.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: desync on the next ancient ruin popped after a load/resync (different reward pool).
fixes.balance: none for a continuous game; after a load ruin rewards follow the documented rules again.

fixes.title: Landmass IDs and continent types change on every load
fixes.before: The exe calls RecalculateLandmasses after loading. FFreeListTrashArray IDs come from a counter that RemoveAll does not rewind, so every landmass and every plot's m_iLandmass got a new ID (+31 generations on lekmod6), and CvLandmass::init cleared the continent type stamped at map generation. Only equality/lookup uses exist, so the game played the same, but a loaded game's map state never matched the continuous one.
fixes.after: The first recalculation after CvMap::Read rewinds the ID counter to the oldest saved landmass generation (the same plot-order recalculation reproduces the saved IDs) and restores the saved continent types. Save format unchanged.
fixes.scope: First RecalculateLandmasses after a map Read; diag trigger FIX id 11. New games and map generation unchanged.
fixes.mp_compat: No simulation difference with golden (IDs only); state digests of mixed peers differ after a load.
fixes.notes: This was the 'per-plot flag word' of host finding 16 (bytes 35..38 of each CvPlot record = m_iLandmass).

fixes.title: Score baseline (m_iMaxPopulation) recomputed from the loaded map
fixes.before: The exe calls InitScoreCalculation after loading; m_iMaxPopulation is derived from the current best nature food yields, so the value saved at game start was replaced by one from the loaded turn (884 -> 880 on lekmod6 T=50). Nothing in the DLL reads it, but the CvGame state of a loaded game differed.
fixes.after: The first initScoreCalculation after CvGame::Read keeps the saved values (m_iMaxPopulation, m_iInit*). Save format unchanged.
fixes.scope: First InitScoreCalculation after a game Read with a non-zero saved m_iMaxPopulation; diag trigger FIX id 12.
fixes.mp_compat: No simulation difference with golden (dead fields); state digests of mixed peers differ after a load.
fixes.notes: getMaxPopulation/getInit* have no gameplay caller (Lua bindings commented out).

fixes.title: Worker AI forced into a re-plan after every load
fixes.before: CvBuilderTaskingAI::Read sets m_iNumCities = -1, so each player's first worker evaluation after a load runs Update(): UpdateRoutePlots refills the shared static m_aiNonTerritoryPlots with that player's road plots (the continuous game still holds the list of the player updated last) and the city best yields are computed at that moment. Until then the best yields (not serialized) were heap garbage.
fixes.after: Once after a load (CvMap::Validate) every player gets m_iNumCities = current count (no forced Update, the static list stays as saved) and its cities' best yields are computed. Save format unchanged.
fixes.scope: First Validate after a map Read; diag trigger FIX id 13 (once per alive player).
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: worker decisions after a load/resync differ.
fixes.notes: Read-side half of DS-0010. Alone it is not exact: the continuous game's best yields date from the owner's turn start (before doTurn re-assigns specializations); FIX-0014 removes that history dependence.

fixes.title: Worker scoring uses city yield deltas from the owner's turn start (not reproducible after a load)
fixes.before: ScorePlot multiplies every worker candidate by the working city's yield deltas and focus yield (CvCityStrategyAI::UpdateBestYields), computed only at the owner's turn start, before doTurn re-assigns city specializations and grows cities. They are not serialized, so a game loaded mid-turn (resync, hot-join, reload) computes other values and its workers choose other builds (measured: Tonga, lekmod6 turn 50: resource weight 18709653 vs 1064777, city focus 2 vs 0). Cities founded mid-turn read garbage.
fixes.after: EvaluateBuilder recomputes the best yields of the owner's cities from the current state before scoring, so a continuous and a loaded game score identically. Save format unchanged.
fixes.scope: Every worker evaluation (AI, city-state and automated human workers). Changes continuous AI play: worker scoring now uses up-to-date specializations and yields instead of the turn-start snapshot.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: desync as soon as a worker decision depends on the refreshed values (every game).
fixes.balance: sim: AI worker build choices change (fresher city focus data); no rule change.
fixes.notes: No trigger counter: it applies to every evaluation. Cost: one UpdateBestYields per owned city per worker evaluation. Drop it from the release set if continuous-play AI must stay golden; FIX-0013 alone keeps golden play and narrows, but does not close, the post-load difference.

fixes.title: AI units move on another player's (or after a load an empty) tactical analysis map
fixes.before: The tactical analysis map (dominance zones, friendly/enemy cell strengths from one player's point of view) is a single global object, built in doTurnPostDiplomacy for each player at its turn start and never serialized. With simultaneous AI turns all AIs are activated in a shuffled order, so every AI's tactical and homeland AI moved units on the map of the player activated last (measured: a city-state's). After a load (resync, hot-join, reload) the map was empty until the next turn, so the loaded game's units moved differently (measured: lekmod6 load at turn 100, Bolivian archer, no sync-RNG difference).
fixes.after: CvPlayerAI::AI_unitUpdate rebuilds the map for the moving player from the current state before its units move (the call Firaxis left commented out, made unconditional), so continuous and loaded games use the same map. Save format unchanged.
fixes.scope: Every AI_unitUpdate that is not blocked by a busy unit/city (AI and automated human units). Changes continuous AI play in simultaneous-turn games: each AI now uses its own, current map.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: desync as soon as an AI unit move depends on the map (every game with fighting).
fixes.balance: sim: AI tactical/homeland moves change (own perspective instead of the last-activated player's); no rule change.
fixes.notes: No trigger counter (applies to every unit update). Cost: one map build per AI_unitUpdate call; no slowdown visible in the 150-turn runs (mean turn time 574 vs 741 ms lekmod6, 511 vs 587 ms pangaea6, parallel, noisy). Confirmed by experiment: rebuilding the map after load for the last-activated player (26) alone made turns 101..102 identical.

fixes.title: Warmonger penalty for city conquest is 0 after a load (EstimatedNumCities not saved)
fixes.before: CvWorldInfo::writeTo/readFrom (pregame world info, saved with every game and synced in the MP lobby) do not carry m_iEstimatedNumCities, the BNW column that CvDiplomacyAIHelpers::GetWarmongerOffset divides by. After a load the value is whatever the process held before: 0 in a fresh process, so conquering or liberating a city changes no warmonger amount and AI opinions of the conqueror stay friendly; a peer with a different history (setup screen, previous game) gets another value. Measured: pangaea6 load at turn 100, player 5 takes a city at turn 129: continuous run +666 warmonger for every observer, loaded run +0; the loaded game diverges at turn 130 (player 4's approach order).
fixes.after: CvWorldInfo::readFrom (and the version-0 reader) re-read EstimatedNumCities from the Worlds row of the loaded world size ID. The value is a pure function of the world size, identical to what a new game caches, so continuous play is unchanged and a loaded game applies the same warmonger penalties. Save format unchanged.
fixes.scope: Every CvWorldInfo read (game load, resync, MP lobby pregame sync) whose held value differs from the database row (diag trigger FIX id 16). Gameplay changes only in loaded games, at the first city conquest or liberation by a major civ.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: desync at the first city conquest after a load or lobby sync where the golden peer holds 0 or a stale value.
fixes.balance: none for a continuous game; in a loaded game the intended warmonger penalty for conquest/liberation is back (a loaded game used to forgive conquests).
fixes.notes: Only reader of the field: GetWarmongerOffset (ApplyWarmongerPenalties on conquest, liberation offset in CvPlayer, the two preview strings). CreateCustomWorldSize keeps the template's ID and value, so the database row equals the cached value for custom map sizes too. The fix is on the read side, so it also covers the lobby pregame sync (FAutoArchive of s_worldInfo), which uses the same operator>>.

fixes.title: x87 precision control of the calling thread decides AI choices (FPU_PRECISION_GUARD)
fixes.before: The gamecore runs on the x87 (/fp:strict, no SSE2), so its float results depend on the precision-control field of the control word of the thread that calls into it. 53 bit (the 0x027F default) and 64 bit play identically, 24 bit does not: AI production weights flip around turn 42-44 and the game diverges (measured with civhost --fpu-pc 24). Direct3D 9 without D3DCREATE_FPU_PRESERVE leaves its thread at 24 bit, Direct3D 11 does not: a DX9 peer and a DX11 peer could simulate differently.
fixes.after: Every entry of the exe into the DLL that runs simulation code or loads state (CvDllGame Update / Init / Init2 / DoGameStarted / Read / ReadSupportingClassData / InitScoreCalculation, every CvDllNetMessageHandler::Response*, CvDllPlayer Init / LaterInit / SetTurnActive / Disconnected / Reconnected / Read, CvDllTeam::Read, CvDllMap::Read, CvDllDealAI::DoAcceptedDeal / DoAcceptedDemand, CvDllGameContext::Init) runs under an RAII guard that sets precision control to 53 bit and rounding control to nearest and puts the caller's two fields back on exit. Only bits 8-11 of the x87 control word are touched (fnstcw / fldcw; exception masks and the SSE MXCSR are not).
fixes.scope: A thread whose precision control is not 53 bit / nearest at an entry (diag trigger FIX id 17 counts those entries). At the default 0x027F the guard is one fnstcw and a compare: no write, behaviour identical to a build without it. 64-bit callers are pinned to 53 bit (same simulation, measured).
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: no difference while the golden peer's thread runs at 53/64 bit; a golden peer whose game-core thread is left at 24 bit (DX9 exe, if that is where the device is created) still diverges from this build's peers, so all peers need the build for the fix to hold.
fixes.notes: Name FPU_PRECISION_GUARD. _controlfp_s (MSVCR90) was measured to rewrite the SSE2 rounding bits of MXCSR when _MCW_RC is in the mask (0x3F80 -> 0x1F80), hence plain fnstcw / fldcw on bits 8-11. Whether the real exes ever run the game-core thread at 24 bit is open (needs a reverse-engineering check of the D3D9 device creation thread and a probe of the control word at a real CvGame::update entry); the guard makes the question moot for peers that run this build. Map generation is covered: the Lua map script runs as a callback inside CvDllGame::Init2, so --fpu-pc-global 24 (which changes the map at turn 1 without the guard) is harmless with it. Not covered: Lua-initiated DLL calls made by exe-side code outside the guarded entries (e.g. Events.SequenceGameInitComplete handlers). Guard sites are fenced by #if defined(LEKMOD_HEADLESS_FIX_0017) because the golden build does not include HeadlessFpuGuard.h.

fixes.title: Every spy is flagged for AI reassignment after a load
fixes.before: operator>>(CvEspionageSpy) reads the saved m_bEvaluateReassignment and then sets it to true. On the first espionage AI pass after a load (resync, reconnect, reload) every AI spy that is not in one of its current target cities is pulled out (MoveSpyTo NULL) and reassigned, while the uninterrupted game leaves it where it is. The loaded peer's spy positions, espionage events and the sync RNG stream diverge from the other peers.
fixes.after: The saved flag is kept, so a loaded game continues like the uninterrupted one. Save format unchanged.
fixes.scope: Every CvEspionageSpy read whose saved flag is false (diag trigger FIX id 18). Gameplay changes only in loaded games with spies (Renaissance onwards), at the first espionage AI pass.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: desync at the first espionage AI pass after a load (the golden loader reassigns its spies).
fixes.balance: none for a continuous game; a loaded game no longer reshuffles the AI's spies.
fixes.notes: The flag is otherwise only set by the game's own events (new spy, spy killed/expelled, target lost) and cleared by CvEspionageAI::AttemptToPlaceSpies, so the saved value is exactly what the continuous game uses next. Found by the byte round trip at T=200 (one byte per major civ, after-read).

fixes.title: AI tactical postures restart from scratch after a load (posture history not saved)
fixes.before: CvTacticalAI picks each dominance zone's posture from the zone state and from last turn's posture (m_Postures); several postures are sticky (counterattack, steamroll, sit-and-bombard, ...). m_Postures was never saved, so after any load (resync, reconnect, reload) every AI and city-state zone started from 'no posture' and could pick another one than the uninterrupted game. Measured: lekmod6 loaded at turn 150 or 200, Riga's land zone becomes HEDGEHOG instead of staying COUNTERATTACK, a Riga unit no longer captures a Bolivian worker at turn 204 and the game diverges at turn 205.
fixes.after: Saves carry last turn's postures in an optional trailer after the supporting class data, the last bytes of the save body: u32 magic 'LKTR', u32 container version 1, u32 record count, then records {u32 tag, u32 byte length, payload}; record 'TPOS' = u32 players, per player {i16 player, u16 count, count x {i32 city ID, i16 owner/water, i16 posture}}, only the entries FindPosture can return (first entry per zone key, not NONE). A reader skips unknown records by their length, so later fixes can add records. The exe's body stream cannot report its end, so CvTacticalAI::Write announces the trailer in its unused 'phony' int (0 -> 'LKTR'), which every reader, golden included, reads and discards. A loaded game continues like the uninterrupted one.
fixes.scope: Every save and load. On load the trailer is read only when the marker is present (diag trigger FIX id 19: once per player whose postures were restored); a save without it (golden or older build) loads with empty postures, as a fresh golden process does (an in-process golden reload kept the previous postures). Continuous play is unchanged.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: desync after a resync/reload once a sticky posture matters (the golden peer restarts from no posture). Saves of either build load in the other.
fixes.balance: none for a continuous game; a loaded game keeps the AI's tactical postures instead of resetting them.
fixes.notes: Save format: new saves are the old layout plus the 4-byte marker value in CvTacticalAI's phony int (one per player) and the trailer (296..584 bytes in the smoke runs). Exe check (Ghidra, civ5_exe, read only): the body loader 0x31bfe0 (called only from Resync_LoadGameFromStreamImpl 0x2b6230, i.e. local load, NetLoadGame and NetForceResync resync alike) calls ReadSupportingClassData last and then only map Validate and LogGameState, with no read and no position or remaining-bytes check; the saver 0x3ae0a0 calls WriteSupportingClassData last, then only Flush (0x32d660: deflate sync flush and the final chunk). So an old DLL leaves the trailer unread without effect. The body stream the exe hands to the DLL is its inflating stream (vtable 0xa77708, ctor 0x1d2bd0, 64 KiB chunks): AtEnd (0x24eff0) asks the compressed file stream, GetSizeLeft is the base GetEOF() - GetPosition() with GetEOF (0x39b7a0) = 0x7fffffff, Skip is a no-op, and ReadIt (0x53c30) throws ('Not enough data') past the end. Hence the marker instead of an AtEnd() probe, and unknown records are skipped by reading. civhost feeds each section as its own FMemoryStream (real AtEnd), so it would not catch a DLL relying on AtEnd; FIX-0019 does not. The user's fallback (CvTacticalAI version bump) was not needed and would have broken new saves in old builds.

fixes.title: A human's move or attack order changes AI danger values on that player's machine only (UI path search on the shared IgnoreUnits pathfinder)

fixes.title: Shared pathfinders keep reusing old search trees for the rest of the game once any player had a busy unit (root cause of the DS-0035 class)
fixes.before: CvPlayerAI::AI_unitUpdate switches on the MP cache flag of six global finders (common, IgnoreUnits, tactical analysis, influence, route, water route) and restores it at the end, but returns early in between when the player has a busy unit or city (stock code). After the first such return the flag stayed on for the rest of the session. In a network game the flag is what allows a search to reuse the previous tree, so from then on every search (also between the AI windows: human orders, turn-start processing) could reuse a tree built earlier, even in an earlier turn, and the window starts no longer forced a reset. That history is neither synced nor saved: a local UI-only search on one of these finders (swap check of a move order, FIX-0020; Player:GetRecommendedFoundCityPlots, City:GetBuyPlotCost, Game.GetLongestCityConnectionPlots) replaces the tree on one machine only, and a machine that loads a game (resync, hot join, reload) starts with the flag off and empty finders. Measured trigger in civhost: a human player with an automated unit (so AI_unitUpdate runs for it) while another of its units still has a mission timer; AI units never have one with quick movement (CvUnit::ShowMoves), and AI-only civhost games never hit it (0 times in 100 turns of lekmod6, db and lekmod-mp options).
fixes.after: The early return restores the six flags exactly as the normal exit does. Outside AI_unitUpdate and the CvPlayer::setTurnActive turn-start block a network game now searches from scratch every time, and each of those blocks starts with a forced reset, so a search can reuse only trees built inside the same block from synced state: the same on every machine, unaffected by UI-only searches and by loads.
fixes.scope: AI_unitUpdate of a player with a busy unit or city (diag trigger FIX id 25). Changes synced play after the first such return: the reuse decisions of later searches (network games: searches outside the blocks are fresh; all games: the blocks start with a reset again). Expected and intended; human-player sessions differ from the unfixed build from that point (e.g. the DS-0035 trap trajectory at turn 58, the stale turn-57 tree reuse).
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with a build without FIX-0025: desync once any player's AI_unitUpdate returns early on a busy unit (from then on the unfixed peer reuses trees the fixed peer does not). All peers must run the same build.
fixes.balance: none (pathfinding results only differ where a stale tree was reused; no rule or value change)
fixes.notes: The only SetMPCacheSafe(true) sites are AI_unitUpdate and the bDoTurn block of CvPlayer::setTurnActive; the latter has no exit between set and restore (doTurn, doTurnUnits). Both save and restore the previous state, so nested blocks stay correct. SetMPCacheSafe sets m_bForceReset whenever the state changes, which is what makes each block start fresh once the flag is off between blocks. The forced resets of the common, IgnoreUnits, route and water route finders at the start of AI_unitUpdate are unchanged; tactical analysis and influence had none. With FIX-0025 a UI-only search can no longer reach a synced search in a network game (the next synced search is either outside the blocks and fresh, or the first of a block and reset); FIX-0020 is kept as defence in depth. The three UI getters named in the campaign notes (GetRecommendedFoundCityPlots, GetBuyPlotCost, GetLongestCityConnectionPlots) did not change synced state in any civhost probe, with or without this fix, even with the flags stuck from turn 1 (see evidence); the demonstrated UI path stays the swap check.

fixes.title: ResponseResearch with a tech id past the table crashes every machine
fixes.before: A research command whose tech id is past the tech table (normal research, not a free tech or a steal) reached CvPlayerTechs::CanEverResearch -> GC.getTechInfo, which indexes the table unchecked: every machine crashed. FIX-0101 range-checks the tech only in the espionage branch.
fixes.after: Such commands are ignored on every machine. Honest commands (a tech from the tree / chooser, or NO_TECH to clear the queue) are unchanged.
fixes.scope: ResponseResearch with eTech < NO_TECH or eTech >= number of techs (any branch), or an invalid player id.
fixes.mp_compat: Mixed with golden: the golden peers crash on such a command; honest play identical. Class changes sim-compat-id: everybody updates together.
fixes.honest_senders: TechPopup/TechTree (vanilla, EUI, Lekmod UI) send a tech of the table or NO_TECH; the DLL sends none.
fixes.notes: Why FIX-0101 missed it: its tech range test sits inside the steal-branch condition (iDiscover <= 0 && ePlayerToStealFrom != NO_PLAYER); the free branch is safe on its own (CanResearchForFree range-checks), the normal branch is not.

fixes.title: A move order to a plot off the map crashes the owner's machine later
fixes.before: ResponsePushMission queued a MOVE_TO (or ROUTE_TO) whose target plot does not exist.
